notes: Arduino Due is not in the catalogue, so a new arduino-due part type was created (digital 0-13, A0-A11, DAC0/DAC1, GND, 5V, 3.3V, etc.).
The Due is shown beside the breadboard (not plugged in); all connections to it are jumper wires into its header sockets.
Exact breadboard columns/rows are estimated from the picture; the potentiometer sits in columns 16-18 (VCC red, wiper yellow to A0, GND black).

The picture shows the blue pin wires landing on the opposite half of the breadboard from the resistor and power wire. Following the text instead, each button has its input-pin wire and 10K pull-down resistor to ground on the same side (side 1, bottom bank) and the 3.3V wire on the other side (side 2, top bank).
The two long red/black wires on the left link the top and bottom power/ground rails. The red wire carries 3.3V from the Due and the black wire carries GND.
DAC0 and DAC1 are outputs only (for an optional oscilloscope) and have no wires in the circuit.
